title: Man Utd v Brentford: Key stats and talking points - Yahoo Sports
content: Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first home game as Manchester United boss as they look to move out of the relegation places against Brentford. BBC Sport takes a look at the key themes going into the game. Pochettino has experienced quite a lot in football - but his opening week in charge of Manchester United really has been quite something. There have been red cards, rescinded red cards, disallowed goals, two penalties in 76 seconds, six goals conceded, bobbles and divots. His side's defeat by Liverpool and draw with Sporting had it all. The Argentine needs to try to restore some calm if he is to haul his side out of the bottom three. However, the stats continue to mount up: Nine games without a Premier League win is their longest in the top flight since an 11-game run between November 1989 to February 1990; The first time since October 1986 they have played three or more consecutive league games starting the day in the bottom three; Their lowest points total (eight) after 11 games of a league campaign since seven in 1972-73 (assuming three points for a win); They have conceded two or more goals in their past five halves of league games - and no Premier League team has ever conceded at least twice in six consecutive halves; They have conceded two or more goals in seven consecutive matches for the first time since November 1977; The 36 goals they have conceded - including 21 in their past seven games - is the most by any side Europe's big five leagues, and their only clean sheet in 17 matches came against Sabah. Pochettino has it all to do, but they can at least fall back on an excellent home record against Brentford in the Premier League - played five, won five. The Bees last won at Old Trafford in 1937. Brentford arrive at Old Trafford fresh from a 4-0 win over Everton, which equalled their biggest Premier League home win - against Manchester United in August 2022. Securing a win at Old Trafford, though, has proved far trickier and the Bees have struggled to pick up wins on the road of late. They have proved hard to beat but are without a victory in their past 10 away league games (D7, L3), dating back to a 4-3 triumph over Burnley nine months ago. It is their longest such run since a 15-game winless away streak between April and December 2018 in the Championship. Head coach Keith Andrews racks up a half century of Premier League games in charge and he must reflect of a job well done so far. Only Brighton (26) and Manchester City (22) have scored more goals than their 20 so far this season, while Brighton are the only side to record more victories by three or more goals. While last season's top scorer Igor Thiago is yet to fire on all cylinders, they have a host of players who are. Summer recruit Jaidon Anthony has four assists in his past five league games, Keane Lewis-Potter's form has earned him a new long-term contract, while the likes of Vitaly Janelt and Michael Kayode continue to impress in Andrews' well-oiled machine. In their win over the Toffees, Brentford attempted 757 passes, with 680 of them successful, both of which were their highest figures in a Premier League game.

title: Austria v Spain: Preview - Davis Cup
content: The last quarter-final tie of the 2026 Davis Cup by Generali Final 8 in Bologna pits Austria against Spain for the first time since 2012. While Austria aims to make their first semi-final in over 25 years (1990), Spain is looking for redemption after falling one tie short of the title in 2025. The two sides will play three matches - two singles followed by a deciding doubles, if required. The winner will face either Germany or Great Britain in Saturday’s semifinal. This will be the sixth meeting for Austria and Spain. While Austria leads the series 3-2, they haven’t scored a win over Spain since 1995, when former world No. 1 Thomas Muster led his team to a 4-1 win in the first round. Their most recent meeting came in the 2012 World Group quarter-finals, where Spain defeated Austria, 4-1. Current captain Jurgen Melzer was part of that team in 2012, and helped lead Austria into the quarter-finals thanks to a surprise win over Russia in the first round. Team: Jurij Rodionov, Lukas Neumayer, Joel Schwaerzler, Neil Oberleitner, Lucas Miedler. History: Austria first competed in Davis Cup in 1905, but their team has never reached a final in 91 years. Their best effort came in 1990, when they upset Spain and blanked Italy 5-0 to reach the semi-finals. Playing in front of a home crowd in Vienna, their tie against the United States came down to a final match; after Thomas Muster blitzed Andre Agassi in straight sets, Michael Chang came back from two sets down to defeat Horst Skoff and deny Austria their first final. Things have begun looking up for Austria of late. The team made it into the Final 8 for a second year in a row after edging past Japan and surprising Belgium in their 2026 qualifying matches. One to watch: Jurij Rodionov has been remarkably clutch in Davis Cup this season, winning all four singles matches against Japan and Belgium. In both ties, he won the decisive match to help his team advance. Team: Carlos Alcaraz, Rafael Jodar, Daniel Merida, Pedro Martinez, Marcel Granollers. History: The Spaniards are six-time Davis Cup champions, with their first victory coming at the dawn of the new millennium. They won four titles in the 2000s and most recently lifted the trophy in 2019 after spending several years in the 2010s outside of World Group action. With Grand Slam-winning players like Carlos Alcaraz on their roster, more success appears likely for Spain in the 2020s, and indeed they came agonizingly close to a seventh title just last year. After battling through both quarter- and semi-final ties against Czechia and Germany, Jaume Munar fell just short of forcing a deciding doubles match to Flavio Cobolli in the championship tie. One to watch: While all eyes will be on Alcaraz, Spain’s fortunes may come down to Rafael Jodar, a 20-year-old finishing up a breakthrough 2026 season. Like Alcaraz, he competed in last week’s Nitto ATP Finals in Turin. Jodar made his Davis Cup debut earlier this year, where he helped lead Spain to a 4-0 win over Chile to book their spot in the Final 8. Click here to find out how to follow all the action

title: Martin v. United States Brief: Raiding the Wrong House Is Not a Policy Judgment Conferring Immunity on Government Agents - Cato Institute
content: Sign up to have blog posts delivered straight to your inbox! In the early morning hours of October 18, 2017, an FBI SWAT team broke down the front door of the Atlanta home Curtrina Martin shared with her partner, Hilliard Cliatt, and her seven-year-old son. Curtrina and Hilliard hid in their bedroom closet as agents in helmets and ballistic vests stormed into their room with rifles. Across the hall, Curtrina’s son lay awake and terrified. After dragging Hilliard out of the closet and handcuffing him on the bedroom floor, Special Agent Lawrence Guerra noticed that Hilliard didn’t match the description of the man they had come to arrest. That man lived three houses away, on a different street. Agent Guerra had a GPS, a phone with Google Maps, and text alerts pinging the target’s location every fifteen minutes. Still, no one checked the address before breaking in. Curtrina Hilliard and Curtrina’s son sued under the FTCA, but the panel held that the discretionary-function exception barred their claims. It “reluctantly” concluded it could not revisit circuit precedent on whether the exception shields unconstitutional conduct. However, all three judges joined a concurrence calling this case “a good vehicle” for reconsideration. Cato filed an amicus brief, joined by the Law Enforcement Action Partnership (LEAP) and the Rutherford Institute, asking the court to grant en banc rehearing and hold that discretion in conducting a raid does not shield a failure to confirm the address before entering. title: Sutton's predictions: Ipswich v Aston Villa - Yahoo Sports
content: I actually think Aston Villa will win this game 2-1 but I want to make it clear the scoreline I have gone for is from my commentary colleague, Alistair Bruce-Ball, who is an Ipswich fan - a fake one, but still a fan. I asked him about this game when we were in Belgium for Liverpool's Champions League game on Wednesday. He will be at Portman Road on Saturday for BBC Radio 5 Live and he is backing the Tractor Boys to get something, so I am doing the same out of respect for him. Ipswich really need a result too. They have gone five league games without a win and, with Hull City and Coventry City both winning last week, they are the lowest placed of the promoted sides. That is never a good thing, and it feels like Gary O'Neil's side are in a precarious position at the moment, where they are getting sucked towards the bottom three. I've been surprised to see Villa hit a bit of a sticky patch too, with three successive league draws and no wins in six, so it will be interesting to see if they are any better here.

title: Sutton's predictions: Man Utd v Brentford - Yahoo Sports
content: I am at this game for BBC Radio 5 Live and I am not expecting much to change for Manchester United. No-one thought it was going to be easy for Mauricio Pochettino to go in at United and turn things around. He has taken over a complete rabble. United's draw in Lisbon on Wednesday was chaotic, but you also have to consider how Sporting have not got going in the Portuguese league or the Champions League this season. That was not a great Sporting side. They are pretty average and Brentford will be a much bigger test. The Bees are supremely well-organised and will be full of confidence, too, after putting four goals past Everton on Monday. They were against 10 men for the entire second half, but were 2-0 up by then anyway. Pochettino needs something to cling to, but picking that backline must be like pinning the tail on the donkey for him. Whoever he picks, they are not very good. I really want to be more positive about United, because I heard from quite a few of their fans last weekend, but this prediction is about as positive as I can be about them at the moment.

title: Czechia v Canada: Preview - Davis Cup
content: The opening tie of the 2026 Davis Cup by Generali Final 8 in Bologna pits Czechia against Canada for the very first time. While Canada seeks to make a first semi-final since winning it all in 2022, it’s been an even longer road back for the Czechs, who have been shut out of the semi-finals for over a decade. The two sides will play three matches - two singles followed by a deciding doubles, if required. The winner will face either Italy or Korea, Rep. in Friday’s semifinal. This will be the debut meeting for Czechia and Canada. Team: Jiri Lehecka, Jakub Mensik, Tomas Machac, Patrik Rikl, Adam Pavlasek History: Champions for the first time in 1980, Czechia became a Davis Cup powerhouse at the end of the 2000s, roaring into their first final in nearly three decades in 2009. Three years later, they won the first of two back-to-back titles in 2012 and 2013. Led by future captain Tomas Berdych, the Czechs earned thrilling 3-2 wins over Spain and Serbia, with both ties coming down to the final rubber. Their 2014 bid for a three-peat ended in the semifinals, and by the end of the decade, they had fallen out of the World Group entirely. Back on the main stage in Bologna, the Czechs bring a strong line-up to the Finals after a pair of wins in the qualifiers. In September, Jiri Lehecka and Jakub Mensik teamed up to defeat the United States for a second year in a row to book their ticket to the Final 8. One to watch: Jiri Lehecka carries plenty of energy into the Davis Cup Finals after a slew of quality results this fall. The 25-year-old made his first Masters 1000 final at the Miami Open and made two more finals in the last month. With a 14-7 record in Davis Cup singles matches, Lehecka is 3-0 in 2026, scoring crucial victories over Ben Shelton and Learner Tien to lead Czechia into the Finals. Team: Felix Auger-Aliassime, Liam Draxl, Alexis Galarneau, Duncan Chan, Keegan Rice History: Canada first joined Davis Cup in 1913 and finally came of age in 2022 when they lifted their first-ever Davis Cup trophy. The victory was a culmination of a ten-year climb that began in 2013, when they shocked Spain en route to the semifinals. They fell just short of the title in 2019 but got their revenge just three years later when Felix Auger-Aliassime scored a key win over Carlos Alcaraz in group play, who rode that momentum to a flawless performance in the knockout stage. After nearly falling out of the World Group in 2025, Canada is back in the mix in 2026, winning two home ties over Brazil and France. Against the latter, Auger-Aliassime nabbed decisive wins over Quentin Halys and Arthur Rinderknech. One to watch: Speaking of Auger-Aliassime, the 26-year-old proved toughest to beat indoors this season, winning his ninth career singles title in Montpellier and reaching a 22nd career final the following week in Rotterdam. Peaking at No. 4 in the rankings in June, the Montreal native will aim to end his 2026 season on a high note against the likes of Lehecka and Mensik, against whom he owns a combined 4-2 head-to-head. title: Trial in the case of The Prosecutor v. Rodrigo Roa Duterte to open on 30 November - | International Criminal Court
content: On 30 November 2026 at 10:00 (The Hague local time), the trial in the case The Prosecutor v. Rodrigo Roa Duterte will open before Trial Chamber III of the International Criminal Court (ICC). Mr Duterte is charged with crimes against humanity of murder and attempted murder, allegedly committed as part of a widespread and systematic attack against a civilian population in the Philippines between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019. The hearings are scheduled to take place from 30 November 2026 onwards. Daily hearings will, in principle, run from 10:00 to 11:00; 11:30 to 12:30; 13:30 to 14:30; 15:00 to 16:00 (The Hague Local time). The hearing can be followed with a 30-minute delay on the ICC website (Courtroom I), as well as on the ICC Facebook and YouTube accounts. On Monday 30 November, the Judges will first verify that Mr Duterte understands the nature of the charges and will ask him whether he makes an admission of guilt or pleads not guilty to the charges. The Chamber will then hear the opening statements of the parties and participants. The Chamber set the following schedule for the opening statements: Thereafter the Chamber will immediately commence with the testimony of the first Prosecution witness. title: Italy v Czechia: Preview - Davis Cup
content: In the first semi-final at the 2026 Davis Cup by Generali Final 8, three-time defending champions Italy face a talented Czechia side looking to return to the final for the first time since winning back-to-back titles in 2012-13. After contrasting victories in their opening matches of the week, the European duo return to centre stage to renew a near-century-old rivalry. Hosts Italy edged past an inspired Korea, Rep. in their quarter-final on Wednesday and will know that Tomas Berdych’s talented Czech side is likely to present an even sterner test. The two teams will play three matches – two singles followed by a deciding doubles, if required. The winner will face either Great Britain or Spain in Sunday’s final. This will be the 12th time the two teams have faced off in the Davis Cup, nearly a century after first crossing paths. Italy won on that occasion, fighting back to win 3-2 on home soil in the Europe Zone final of the 1928 competition. Since then, though, the Czechs have dominated the rivalry, prevailing in eight of the next 10, including during the title runs of 1980 and 2012. In the latter of these, current captain Tomas Berdych played a central role, winning both his matches to help seal a 4-1 World Group first-round triumph in Ostrava. Team: Flavio Cobolli, Luciano Darderi, Lorenzo Musetti, Matteo Berrettini, Andrea Vavassori History: At this year’s Final 8, Italy will bid for a fourth consecutive Davis Cup title and become the first nation to achieve the feat since the early 1970s. The all-conquering USA was the last side to enjoy such a spell of dominance, although their achievement is caveated by it coinciding with the transition away from the Challenge Round format whereby the defending champion advanced directly to the following year’s final. Wednesday’s hard-fought win extended their current unbeaten run to 15 ties, a sequence stretching back to 2023’s round-robin stage. One to watch: Initially omitted from the Italian team, Matteo Berrettini was a late replacement for Simone Bolelli. His presence further bolsters an already powerful unit, bringing the experience from the title-winning campaigns of 2024 and 2025 and a 10-match winning streak in the competition. Team: Jiri Lehecka, Jakub Mensik, Tomas Machac, Patrik Rikl, Adam Pavlasek History: Czechia, who first won the World Cup of Tennis as Czechoslovakia in 1980, emerged as a Davis Cup powerhouse in the late 2000s. In 2009, they ended a near-three-decade wait to reach a final, before lifting back-to-back titles in 2012 and 2013. Led by future captain Berdych, the Czechs beat Spain and Serbia in the championship matches those years, with both ties coming down to the final rubber. Their 2014 bid for a hat-trick ended in the semi-finals, and by the end of the decade, they had fallen out of the World Group entirely. Buoyed by the emergence of Jiri Lehecka and Jakub Mensik, in recent years they have reemerged as a force. Berdych’s side lost to Spain in the 2025 quarter-finals when fancied to go far and return to Bologna with a point to prove. One to watch: It can only be the talismanic Jiri Lehecka, who improved his record in the competition to 4-0 this season – and 15-7 overall – by beating Felix Auger-Aliassime earlier in the week. The 25-year-old has also impressed on tour of late, building on his runner-up finish at the Miami Masters 1000 with two further finals in the past month.

title: Album Review: DOWN – Volume V - New Noise Magazine
content:
DOWN are among the cult bands of cult bands. Sludge metal is already a niche genre that took multiple headbanging fuckups with punk roots and a penchant for herbs and opioids and celebrating the “Sabbath” to give it a voice and sound emanating that humid, swampy bayou atmosphere effectively making New Orleans its epicenter. DOWN are a supergroup who emerged from those swampy depths in 1991 as a concoction that featured the best of what the scene had to offer consisting of Kirk Windstein and Todd Strange of Crowbar (Strange later replaced by Rex Brown of Pantera, then Pat Bruders of Goatwhore), Pepper Keenan of Corrosion of Conformity, Jimmy Bower of Eyehategod, and Phil Anselmo prior to his joining Pantera. In 1995, they released what was essentially a draft that, to the outside observer, properly represented their scene whose propensity is displayed in its very title—their debut album NOLA. Their scene being very small, being labeled a “supergroup” was incidental as it was just five friends getting together to drink beer, smoke weed, and play music. Each of them stayed occupied with their main projects but always had this to come back to over the last 35 years for whenever they wanted to let loose and do more freestyle writing. In that time, they released four albums, that is if you count the two-part EP DOWN IV, rather irregularly. After 12 years, the longest gap between releases, they are rounding it out to five with Volume V. It’s pretty much classic “metal for good ‘ole boys” for which they’ve come to be known. Written organically through off-the-cuff jam sessions over the course of two days in Anselmo’s home studio “Nodsferatu’s Lair,” the songs are reflective of that fluidity. Nothing feels forced or unsure of itself; it feels like old friends just chillin’ and jammin’. “The Myth” kicks off with those familiar bluesy riffs and beautiful guitar harmonies over groovy rhythms. That classic sludge sound stays consistent throughout the whole album. Keenan and Windstein are having a ball harmonizing their melodies, syncopating their riffs and trading off on leads when it comes time to solo. They recorded their guitar parts at the same time capturing that organic structure that layering can’t replicate. It’s especially prominent in “The Message” and “Twice-Told Tales.” There are some notable escapades to different realms if the song calls for it. “Causeway Grief” is a slower, bluesy ballad with the guitars’ chorus and wah effects creating such a dreary nature that it invokes a scene of driving through wide, open, flat land under a cold and grey sky. Knowing Anselmo, he most likely wrote it while on the road, probably space-cruising, as he croons on about his longing for his hometown. “Blood Oath” also takes its time as the guitar effects in the extensive intro hypnotize you for a good minute-and-a-half before that stomping main riff comes in. Anselmo’s vocal delivery is more reserved with slight distortion, like what you’d hear in classic doom metal, further enhancing the song’s theme of conducting a ritual. That’s another thing: Most of these songs’ lyrical themes deal in horror and occultist elements. “The Myth” makes references to Azrael – one of the four archangels in Islam who assists in the creation and death of man. It’s sung in the first person but changes the perspective midway through. It does invoke an interesting concept of who we consider to be our saviors. “They Walk the Night” depicts two priests ironically becoming possessed after botching an exorcism and wreak blasphemous mayhem all over their village. “Turn Out the Light” reads like Anselmo just took a fat rip and is about to drift off to sleep until, in the final chorus, he starts hallucinating—“there is a demon at the foot of my bed/there is a fire glowing/I’m feeling fine/turn out the light.” Maybe he just saw the ghost of Ozzy. Speaking of which, they wrote “Ozz”, an acoustic ballad in which everyone sings their praises for the Prince of Darkness holding him in a higher, divine image as we all do. Keeping in the incidental theme of songs whose titles reference musical legends with a paranormal aura—“Merciful Fate”. This presented the unlikely collaboration of Anselmo with his deep, rugged, gruff, southern drawl meeting the haunting, ethereal, soprano wails of King Diamond, composing the score of what feels like being in a haunted plantation manor. Despite that, it isn’t exactly a spooky tune. It’s more about Anselmo reminiscing about how reckless and careless he was in his youth, and that his present state of grace is what he considers to be his “merciful fate”. You get that vibe also in songs like “The Message,” “Twice-Told Tales,” “Causeway Grief,” and even a bit in “The Myth” if you read its lyrics as more of a concept—looking back on the lives that they’ve lived and pondering what it’s amounted to for them as individuals. Really, that’s the most honest part about this album—All these guys have been at it for 35 plus years writing this type of music and watching the ebbs and flows of its popularity. Now, sludge metal was never exactly “popular”, but it seems to have gained some newfound attention lately with Anselmo reuniting what’s left of Pantera, the unlikely virality of Crowbar’s song “Repulsive in its Splendid Beauty” and the “Crowbar Cat” memes circling around in social media. That’s the big takeaway from Volume V—Sludge metal is like comfort food in that you generally know what you’re going to get when you hear one of its bands. DOWN hold true to that sentiment because that is the energy that each member brings to the studio. You’re generally going to get a very similar dish from every DOWN album and that includes this one. DOWN, much like the genre they represent, are self-contained and don’t concern themselves with reinventing the wheel. Coming back for the same meal isn’t inherently a bad thing—Maybe there’s something there that you didn’t appreciate the first time or maybe there’s a slight tweak in the recipe—just so long as it still tastes good. DOWN’s Volume V was produced by Eddie Mapp and DOWN, mixed by Dave Fortman, and mastered by Maor Appelbaum at Maor Appelbaum Mastering in California.
